sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct used in published experiments (co-IP, cell-based assays) without reported loss of surface expression or function; no dedicated functional rescue assay quoted in the ledger clip itself.
sites.rationale: RYK is a type I single-pass receptor with a signal peptide spanning residues 1–25 (authoritative landmarks); the mature extracellular N-terminus begins at residue 26. An 'amino-terminal' tag on the full-length membrane-anchored protein can only reside at this single extracellular terminus — upstream of residue 26 would be cleaved with the signal peptide. Python lookup confirms residue 25 = P and residue 26 = P; the junction is 205 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. Position is topology-derived because the clip names no specific residue. Full-length human RYK bearing an amino-terminal 2× Myc epitope tag (pcDNA3.Myc2.hRYK) expressed in mammalian cells; construct described in PMC3776778 as previously published and actively used in co-immunoprecipitation and cell-based experiments.

sources.claim: Full-length human RYK with an amino-terminal 2× Myc epitope tag (pcDNA3.Myc2.hRYK) was described previously [17] .

literature_notes: L1 (FLAG at human RYK residues 598–599) and L2 (FLAG at mouse Ryk codons 585–586) both fall in the intracellular kinase domain (topology landmarks place intracellular domain at 251–607); they are recorded in other_positions. L4 corroborates the same intracellular C-terminal FLAG strategy as L2 but names no specific residue and is therefore subsumed by L2 in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion in the extracellular domain (residues 26–230) other than the N-terminal Myc tag of L3. The extracellular domain of RYK contains a WNT-binding Frizzled-like cysteine-rich domain; no internal loop insertion within it is supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG epitope inserted between residues 598 and 599 of full-length human RYK (NP_002949.2); position 598 falls in the intracellular kinase domain (topology 251–607), not on the extracellular face.

FLAG epitope inserted between codons 585 and 586 of mouse Ryk (NP_038677.3) in the Myc2.Ryk.FLAG.CT construct; the equivalent human position (585) is intracellular, confirming this is a cytoplasmic C-terminal tag, not a surface tag.
